planting.note: Direct sow in fall in lean, fast-draining sandy or gravelly soil in full sun; desert milkweed is native to washes and dry slopes of the Mojave, Sonoran, and Colorado Deserts and benefits from the natural winter-spring rainfall cycle of its habitat to establish before summer heat.

directions: Plant in lean, fast-draining sandy or gravelly soil in full sun; desert milkweed is an erect perennial with pale, whitish-green to gray-green foliage and rounded umbels of cream to pale yellow flowers from spring into summer and sometimes fall. Native to dry washes, desert scrub, and Joshua tree woodland of the Mojave, Sonoran, and Colorado Deserts of southern California, Arizona, and northern Baja California, it is exceptionally drought tolerant once established and needs little to no supplemental summer water. Like other milkweeds it is a larval host plant for monarch butterflies and an important nectar source for native desert pollinators. Avoid rich soil or regular irrigation, which shorten its life and encourage rank, weak growth; established plants may go dormant in extended drought and resprout with rain.

common_name: Milk Chocolate New Zealand Hair Sedge

planting.note: Set out divisions or container plants in spring in moist, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; sharp winter drainage matters more to this sedge's survival than cold air temperatures.

directions: Plant in moist, fertile, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade. Milk Chocolate forms a dense, cascading tussock of hair-fine foliage in a distinctive warm chocolate-brown with a subtle pink tinge, shifting toward orange and brown tones as autumn approaches. Its fine texture and unusual color make it an effective accent at the front of a border, in a container, or massed as a small-scale groundcover alongside silver- or chartreuse-leaved companions. Comb out dead blades by hand in early spring rather than shearing, and divide congested clumps every few years to maintain vigor and color.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in moist, well-drained soil in partial shade to full sun in spring; Coca-Cola produces fine, curling foliage in a deep cola-brown that darkens further through the season.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained soil in partial shade to full sun. Coca-Cola is a New Zealand sedge selected for its fine, thread-like foliage in a deep, glossy cola-brown, darker and richer than its sibling selection Toffee Twist, forming a loose, cascading, fountain-like mound. It tolerates a range of light from fairly sunny to shaded sites and adapts to both moist and moderately dry soil once established. Comb out old, dead foliage by hand in early spring rather than shearing, and divide congested clumps every few years to keep the mound looking fresh.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring in moist, humus-rich soil in partial to full shade; Lemon Zest spreads slowly by rhizome into a weed-suppressing patch and colors best in bright shade or gentle morning sun rather than hot, direct afternoon exposure.

directions: Plant in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial to full shade. Lemon Zest is a broad-leaved sedge selected for foliage in a vivid, glowing lemon-yellow, a bolder texture and brighter color than the white-margined broadleaf sedge cultivars, making it an eye-catching edging or small-scale groundcover plant among hostas, ferns, and astilbes. Color is most vibrant in bright shade or filtered morning sun with consistent moisture; hot, direct afternoon sun can scorch the bright foliage. Divide congested clumps every few years in spring to maintain vigor.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade in spring; Everlime is an EverColor-series selection with deep green leaves edged in lime-green that holds its color well through the season.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, humus-rich soil in partial shade. Everlime is a low, gently arching EverColor-series sedge selected as a color sport of the popular 'Evergold', with leathery, deep green leaves edged in bright lime-green rather than Evergold's cream-gold margins. Its fine, fountain-like texture pairs well with hostas, heucheras, and ferns at the front of a shaded border or in containers, and it tolerates both consistently moist soil and brief dry spells once established. Evergreen to semi-evergreen in mild climates; comb out old foliage in early spring to keep clumps looking fresh.

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in moist, well-drained, fertile soil in full sun to partial shade in spring; Everglow is an EverColor-series selection whose leaf-margin color shifts seasonally, from cream in spring and summer to orange and then bronze by winter.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained, fertile soil in full sun to partial shade. Everglow is an EverColor-series sedge grown for its slender, dark green leaves with a seasonally shifting margin color: cream from spring through summer, deepening to orange and then bronze as cold weather arrives, before fading back to cream the following year. Its fine, cascading texture suits borders, containers, and shaded edging, and it tolerates a wider range of light than many sedges, from fairly sunny sites to partial shade. Evergreen in mild climates; remove tattered old foliage in summer to keep the clump looking its best.

planting.note: Set out divisions or container plants in spring in moist, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Cappuccino is native to seepages and stream margins in New Zealand and prefers more consistent moisture than many drought-tolerant New Zealand sedges.

directions: Plant in moist, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade with regular moisture. Cappuccino is a New Zealand hair sedge forming a tussock of narrow, arching leaves in warm bronze and chocolate-brown tones reminiscent of its namesake coffee drink. It is native to seepages, pond margins, and stream banks on New Zealand's South Island and does best with more consistent moisture than many of its drought-tolerant New Zealand relatives, though established plants tolerate brief dry spells. Its fine, fountain-like texture works well in containers, border edges, and rain garden plantings. Comb out old foliage by hand in early spring and divide congested clumps every few years to maintain vigor.
